summary: Digby Gut's wooden light, put in operation on 8 July 1901 and deactivated in 2015 after heritage recognition; James Hinds kept it to 1912, then S. Haynes.

notes_for_editor: (1) Page 59 of the 1901 report: the passage sits under the 'NEW AIDS TO NAVIGATION' heading in the Chief Engineer's report, and the report's index lists 'Victoria Beach, New lighthouse, 59'. The corpus marks the printed page '59?' (scan p.74) because the OCR head is not confirmed; the index and the running head agree on 59. (2) S. Haynes: LighthouseFriends is the only source that names him at Victoria Beach. A 1914-report keeper list (OCR columns) puts 'Haynes' fifth, the same position as 'Victoria beach' in the station list; that is a position match only and is not cited. The 1915 list gives 'S. Haynes April 13, 1912' without a station name on the line. (3) The record's 18.3 m focal height conflicts with the 1901 report's 52 ft (15.8 m); corrections lists it. (4) The record's staffing 'automated 1993' comes from Wikidata and was not verified, so the story says nothing about automation. (5) Name trap: the corpus also has a Victoria Beach, Manitoba (a 1915 pole light and a 1922 aerodrome on Lake Winnipeg). None of those entries is this station. (6) No wreck, storm or rescue for this station was found in the corpus, LighthouseFriends or the register, so the story has no 'Storms' chapter. (7) The Parks Canada Directory page for heritage lighthouse 14852 did not render; the register text was read from the Heritage Guide copy. (8) The Pony Express passage and its 230 km figure are LighthouseFriends' description. (9) The 1910 keeper table row for Victoria Beach was checked on the page image (scan p.260, printed p.258): it reads 'Victoria Beach / James Hinds / Mar. 7, 1901 / 130 00', so the name is matched on its own row. (10) The 1901 report gives the tower as 28 ft (8.5 m) to the top of the ventilator; the register gives 8 m (26 ft). The story gives both.
